quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply controlled pressure to both brakes at the same time. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: How do you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most?
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection.
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when choosing a helmet.

questions.question: What can happen if a rider takes a turn too fast?

options.text: The rider may drift into another lane of traffic.
The rider can get through the turn faster.
The rider will keep control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider may drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: How can you make it easier for other drivers to see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle tailgaters?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let them pass. Speeding up can be dangerous because they may continue tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: When a motorcycle rider needs to stop quickly, what should they do?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time to stop quickly. Watch the road ahead to avoid needing emergency stops.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as your motorcycle.
Take it out on the highway right away.
Practice in a controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice in a controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle on the road, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe area first.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you earliest.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic signal.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you earliest.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so other drivers can see you as early as possible when approaching a blind intersection.

questions.question: Why is it difficult to ride right after it starts raining?

options.text: Other drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
The road surface becomes very slippery.
Other drivers go too slowly in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road surface becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the road is especially slippery. Oil from cars has not yet washed away from the pavement, and it mixes with water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: What can you wear to improve your chances of surviving a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: A DOT-approved helmet.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT and state standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality helmet that is properly fastened is the most effective thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when slowing or stopping a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Use the clutch to shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What is true about footrests?

options.text: The driver and passenger can share them.
They are required for the driver and passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required for the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. This keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off as well.

questions.question: How is the risk of head or neck injury reduced?
questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding, no matter how fast you go. Wearing a good-quality helmet properly greatly reduces your risk of head and neck injuries.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may just make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What can help prevent a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use the correct lane position.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, be visible to others, signal your intentions, keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react to changing conditions.

questions.question: When is there less traction for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a motorcycle is leaning.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as in a turn or curve, there is less traction available for braking. You can still use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: Which brakes should you use when stopping?
questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: What can happen from long-term exposure to wind noise?

options.text: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
It is just part of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when you ride. Good ear protection lets you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: What is the center portion of the lane like?

options.text: Has oil and grease but still provides enough grip for safe riding.
Makes it hard for other drivers to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has oil and grease but still provides enough grip for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of each lane. This area usually has enough grip for safe motorcycle riding, unless it is raining.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose, so it flaps in the wind while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly.
questions.explanation: Riding gear should protect you while staying comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snug enough to not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: How should you load saddlebags?

options.text: Distribute weight as evenly as possible between the bags.
Put more weight in one bag than the other.
Put as much weight as possible in one saddlebag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distribute weight as evenly as possible between the bags.
questions.explanation: Saddlebags should have equal weight in each bag. Uneven weight can cause the motorcycle to drift to one side.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.
questions.explanation: When tailgated, ride in a way that encourages the other driver to pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster, which increases danger.
